text:
Maya Chen: FYI — dropping the company-level OKR draft for FY26 Q2 here. Trying to keep the slate tight: 3 objectives + 2 crosscutting reliability KRs. Please call out any must-haves or fatal risks by EOD Thurs.

Maya Chen: Obj A - Deliver predictable low-latency inference for high-throughput customers
KR1: 95th-pctl latency <= 120ms for hosted API at 1k RPS baseline
KR2: Reduce per-token cost by 18% via batching + cache improvements
KR3: Dedicated: ship autoscaling policy and SLA page for early enterprise pilot

Maya Chen: Obj B - Expand private deployment readiness for regulated customers
KR1: VPC control plane GA for 2 pilot customers
KR2: KMS/HSM onboarding flow and audit logs exported to SIEM

Maya Chen: Obj C - Developer-first experience for adoption & evals
KR1: 10 reference apps updated to new SDKs + test harness
KR2: Onboard 5 customers on Optimize recommendations and measure cost savings

Maya Chen: Crosscutting KRs:
- Reliability: 99.9% uptime for hosted control plane (monthly)
- Quality safety: Eval suite regression guardrails in CI with alerting

Arjun Patel: Quick read: these look reasonable. Two asks: 1) the latency KR feels tight given Llama-3 tails — can we make it conditional on model class? 2) How are we measuring per-token cost — with and without cache?

Ben Liu: +1 on conditional latency. Also want a soft KR for streaming UX improvements — even a non-numeric indicator would help prioritize design time.

Leah Ortega: tagging this to exec cadence: we need clarity on tradeoffs that will affect renewals. For Dedicated pilots, customers expect a documented rollback window and a runbook. Can we add a launch criteria checklist?

Maya Chen: Good call. Proposed launch criteria (short):
```
- Performance: meets KR targets for 3-day steady traffic test
- Safety: no regressions on top-100 eval prompts
- Docs: API + migration guide + SLO page published
- Support: on-call runbook, escalation path, and canary rollback plan
- Compliance: required audit artifacts for pilot customers
```

Samira Kahn: From CS backlog — two customers (FinTrust, HealthFlow) made private deployment conditional asks: guaranteed data isolation + SOC2 timeline. If we miss Q2 pilot GA for Private, they will ask for contract clauses. Need this noted as a dependency.

Arjun Patel: On measurement: let's define per-token cost as total infra spend / tokens served with an experimental bucket for when KV cache hit-rate > 40% vs < 40%. We should include a KR for cache hit-rate (e.g., increase hit-rate by 12%) because that directly affects cost.

Maya Chen: Adding cache hit-rate KR and the launch checklist to the doc. Question for execs: do we want to keep 3 objectives or split Private into its own objective if pilots expand? That would push Developer experience work to Q3. Opinions?

Leah Ortega: I'd prefer keeping it consolidated for now; we risk diluting focus if we split. But we need a hard gating policy: if pilots require >2 FTEs from infra next quarter, escalate to sales for support funding.

Ben Liu: Design will scope streaming UX as a 4-week spike in Q2 if we keep it as a soft KR. I'll prepare mockups and perf guardrails.

Maya Chen: Action items:
- Maya: update doc with cache KR + launch checklist (by Thu EOD)
- Arjun: propose measurement queries and test harness for cost calc (Mon)
- Ben: mockups spike plan and acceptance criteria (Mon)
- Samira: confirm FinTrust/HealthFlow contract timelines and escalate if GA slips (Thu)

Maya Chen: Final ask — if no objections, I'm planning to present this at Exec sync next Tue and ask for formal sign-off there. Please react or reply by EOD Thu if you need changes. :pray:

OpsBot: Reminder scheduled — Exec sync presentation slot reserved on Tue 10:00am.

Leah Ortega: :thumbsup: unless something else comes up.

Arjun Patel: :+1: on conditional latency wording and cache KR.

Ben Liu: :thumbsup:

Samira Kahn: Noted — will follow up with CS leads and flag risks.

Maya Chen: Thanks team — I'll post the updated draft after I fold in Arjun's measurement notes.
